text.p: Tropical Cyclone 06B has made landfall in Bangladesh and is weakening. Heavy rains will likely continue over the next 12 hours as the storm dissipates. Flooding is expected with a strong coastal storm surge continuing for the next few hours. The threat to shipping will lessen as the system moves inland and further dissipates.

Tropical Cyclone 05S has formed in the south Indian Ocean and is tracking to the west-southwest. Top winds are near 30-35 mph and very slow strengthening is expected. This storm is a moderate risk to shipping.

Ireland is experiencing winds of 30-40 knots with gusts to 60 knots. Winds are also 25-45 knots with higher gusts in the Irish Sea, the English Channel and the northeast Atlantic. Strong seas are also affecting these areas. Shipping in the region is likely affected. Strong winds may cause damage to property in Ireland, Scotland and England this period as this storm moves across. This storm was formerly Hurricane Lili when it was out over the central Atlantic late last week and originated in the western Caribbean.
